grader.finalMessage:
Run `2026-10-10_0630_mcp-recipe_haiku-5.5-high` (Haiku 5.5, high effort, MCP Recipe test) scored **94.5 / 100**. All 43 automated checks passed. The grade is written to `grade.json` and `grade.md`, the run shows up in the report's Grade table, and after the reset `npm run status` says **pristine**.

| Category | Score |
|---|---|
| It works | 35 / 35 |
| Content modeling | 24 / 25 |
| Code architecture & conventions | 24.5 / 25 |
| Content & presentation | 6.5 / 10 |
| Process & honesty | 4.5 / 5 |

**Summary:** The model built a complete, working blog through the two Umbraco MCP servers only. It has a front page with styled post cards (image, date, title, excerpt) and two posts built with the block grid. The schema, the block-rendering code and the project conventions all follow the rules. The weak part is the writing: the posts are short, and the post titled "three reasons" only gives two.

**Top issues:**
1. **Thin posts:** each has about four short paragraphs. `/three-reasons-mcp-is-worth-the-fuss/` also says MCP tools always ask for confirmation before publishing or deleting, which isn't something the protocol guarantees.
2. **No shared layout:** both page views (`blogFrontPage.cshtml`, `blogPost.cshtml`) repeat the whole HTML page structure instead of sharing a layout, and the post pages have no site header or navigation.
3. **Alt text:** the image block uses the photo credit as the image's alt text.
4. **File outside the project:** one curl command wrote `/tmp/x`. The model noticed, deleted it and said so in its report, so it cost 0.5 points.
5. **Small block set:** only rich text, image and quote, with no block settings. One of the five imported photos isn't used.

The 10 build warnings are all security advisories on an image-processing package (SixLabors.ImageSharp) that came with the scaffold, so I didn't count them against the model. The model's final report was accurate.

The `gradedAt` timestamp in `grade.json` is an approximate time I filled in, not the exact moment of grading.
